event.description: Reduce the factorized positional representation from rank 3 to rank 2 while retaining the rank-6 tied token subspace, distinct seven segment codes, digit-index sharing, full QKV attention, shared no-offset normalization, reversed operands, d=14, two blocks, ff=19, and the 45000-step schedule.
event.proposal: Family: position representation. Retained incumbent is attempt-0051 with 2944 parameters at 99.440000%, a +0.440000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the most recent accepted positional result is attempt-0045, rank-3 digit-index plus segment factorization (2980, 99.96%); the most recent rank-2 failure is attempt-0036, a reversed-input but unfactorized 35-row rank-2 position table, an optimization failure; 13 prior position-representation macro attempts plus a rank-7 schedule reattempt. The immediately preceding rank-5 token candidate attempt-0052 is an optimization failure (45000 steps, 98.3% peak validation, no checkpoint), not a scored nonqualification. Hypothesis: explicit digit-index and segment sharing concentrates the necessary positional distinctions enough that two latent coordinates can now suffice, unlike the former independent per-position table. Reducing rank from 3 to 2 changes the factorized positional code tables and projection from 11x3 plus 7x3 plus 3x14 to 11x2 plus 7x2 plus 2x14, lowering actual parameters from 2944 to 2912. This is a positional-subspace representation reduction, not scalar pruning. It is more informative than rank 1 because it tests the immediate lower boundary of the accepted factorized representation rather than a qualitatively collapsed code space.
